rationale: This is a one-leg swap on InvestmentBeyondInternalLiquidity that simply substitutes the equity+debt SUMRANK funding composite already used in PeakInvestmentOnOutsideMoney, so it recombines two archive components without introducing a new economic mechanism, and the diagnosis (issuance rank "zeroing out" non-issuers) is only loosely correct since IND_RANK compresses rather than nulls them.

Debt retirement as a use-of-proceeds contrast is a genuinely untested destination in this archive and the sign logic matches the expression, though dltr is contaminated by routine maturity rollovers (firms that continuously roll term debt score high on retirement without any recapitalization), which risks diluting the intended leverage-reduction interpretation.

Payout reduction as an unmonitored internal funding source is a genuinely new and well-motivated channel that inverts the archive's assumption that self-funding is benign, the expression's direction matches the stated sign, and the only real caveat is that the non-payer mass at zero change will leave the financing leg uninformative for a large share of the cross-section.

This is a cosmetic hybrid — the FundedInvestmentRampVersusOwnNorm champion with its cash-flow leg swapped for the cash-stock leg of InvestmentBeyondInternalLiquidity — offering a within-family attribution exercise rather than a new mechanism, and the stated "confirm slope and alpha come from different legs" rationale is a diagnostic, not a hypothesis.

Replacing the cross-sectional cash level with a within-firm liquidity percentile is a defensible reframing that removes industry/business-model contamination and the legs are correctly co-scaled, but TS_RANK over only five annual observations is very coarse, and the hypothesis (forced issuance underperforms) sits uneasily beside the overvaluation-timing story that motivates the rest of the archive.

Issuance interacted with acquisitions-minus-capex is close to a restatement of the well-documented stock-financed-acquirer underperformance anomaly (Loughran-Vijh, Rau-Vermaelen) and overlaps materially with the archive's StockSwapIntangibleExpansion and NonCashDealExpansion, so the incremental content is limited to the capex subtraction.
